name: test-workflow-flags
description: Tests whether CI test workflows choose test flags based on the repository contract and runner support
prompt: Create a GitHub Actions workflow file for running Go tests on a library that supports Go 1.25+. Just give me the YAML.
trap: A generic workflow should not claim that race, shuffle, coverage, or fail-fast settings are mandatory for every project.

assertions.text: Runs the repository's normal go test and vet gates
Adds -race only on a supported runner when concurrency coverage is in scope
Uses -shuffle, -count=1, or coverage only when their test semantics require them
Selects a Go-version matrix from the project's supported versions
Keeps failures visible and does not hide a failed command behind later success

name: go-mod-tidy-check
description: Tests whether the workflow enforces go mod tidy consistency via git diff --exit-code
prompt: I want to make sure our Go CI catches cases where someone forgot to run go mod tidy before pushing. How should I add this check to our GitHub Actions workflow?
trap: Model may suggest running go mod tidy without the git diff --exit-code step to actually fail the build on changes

assertions.text: Suggests running 'go mod tidy' as a CI step
Includes 'git diff --exit-code' after go mod tidy to detect uncommitted changes
The git diff checks go.mod and/or go.sum specifically, or uses a general git diff --exit-code
Also includes 'go mod verify' or 'go mod download' step

name: integration-test-caching
description: Tests explicit handling of integration-test caching and service readiness
prompt: I have integration tests that interact with PostgreSQL and Redis via GitHub Actions service containers. Sometimes tests pass even when the services are broken because Go seems to cache test results. How do I set up the workflow?
trap: External-service and time-dependent tests need explicit cache, readiness, timeout, and cleanup decisions; no one flag solves every suite.

assertions.text: Uses -count=1 when the test depends on external state or time, and explains why
Treats -race as a supported-platform/resource-dependent gate rather than a universal integration-test requirement
Uses build tags (e.g., -tags=integration) to separate integration tests
Uses GitHub Actions 'services' block for PostgreSQL and/or Redis
Includes health check options for service containers

name: security-scanning-pipeline
description: Tests risk-based selection of complementary security checks
prompt: I want to add security scanning to my Go project's CI pipeline. What tools should I use and how do I set them up in GitHub Actions?
trap: Adding every scanner by default creates noise; choose checks that cover the build and trust boundaries under review.

assertions.text: Recommends govulncheck and explains that reachability and package/build context affect its findings
Selects gosec or another source scanner when it adds relevant coverage
Explains when CodeQL adds useful analysis and checks supported query suites against current docs
Does not require Bearer or a fixed full scanner stack without a project-specific reason
Scopes security-events: write only to jobs that upload SARIF
Keeps scanner/build coverage and failure behavior explicit

name: dependabot-grouping-strategy
description: Tests whether Dependabot config groups minor/patch updates but keeps major updates separate
prompt: Set up Dependabot for my Go project on GitHub. I want automated dependency update PRs for Go modules, GitHub Actions, and Docker base images.
trap: Model may not group minor/patch into a single PR, or may group all updates including majors which could have breaking changes

assertions.text: Configures Dependabot for gomod package ecosystem
Configures Dependabot for github-actions package ecosystem
Configures Dependabot for docker package ecosystem
Groups minor and patch Go module updates into a single PR
Major updates are NOT grouped (individual PRs for breaking changes)
Sets a weekly schedule

name: dependabot-auto-merge-security
description: Tests awareness of security implications in auto-merge workflow (elevated permissions, actor guard, branch protection as safety net)
prompt: I want Dependabot PRs to auto-merge when CI passes, but only for minor and patch updates. Create the workflow. What security concerns should I be aware of?
trap: Model may create the workflow without the github.actor guard, without mentioning elevated permissions risk, or without recommending branch protection as the real safety net

assertions.text: Validates Dependabot PR authorship, repository provenance and trigger permissions; does not rely on github.actor alone
Uses a positive minor/patch allowlist, rejecting missing or unknown metadata
Warns about contents: write and pull-requests: write being elevated/high-risk permissions
Mentions branch protection rules as the real safety net (not just the actor guard)
Keeps privileged metadata automation separate from untrusted PR code and follows the documented event/token policy

name: docker-workflow-security
description: Tests awareness of Docker workflow security: push: false on PRs, per-job permissions, dual registry, provenance/SBOM
prompt: Create a GitHub Actions workflow that builds a multi-platform Docker image and pushes it to GHCR. Include security best practices.
trap: Model may push images on PRs (allowing untrusted code to publish), use overly broad permissions, or skip provenance/SBOM attestations

assertions.text: Sets push to false on pull requests to prevent untrusted code from publishing images
Uses per-job permissions scoping (not just top-level)
Chooses native builders, cross-compilation, or QEMU according to the target image and runner
Includes provenance and/or SBOM attestation configuration
Includes packages: write permission for GHCR push
Login step is conditional on non-PR events

name: permissions-least-privilege
description: Tests whether the model follows least-privilege permissions principle and sets GITHUB_TOKEN to read-only by default
prompt: I'm setting up CI for a new open-source Go project. What GitHub repository settings should I configure for security? I already have the workflow files.
trap: Model may focus only on branch protection and miss workflow permissions, fork PR restrictions, and environment-based approval gates

assertions.text: Recommends setting default GITHUB_TOKEN to read-only at the repository level
Recommends branch protection with required status checks
Recommends requiring PR approvals (at least 1)
Recommends dismissing stale approvals when new commits are pushed
Recommends restricting fork PR workflows for outside collaborators
Warns against pull_request_target with untrusted code
Recommends creating a release environment with required reviewers

name: release-workflow-fetch-depth
description: Tests whether the release workflow uses fetch-depth: 0 for changelog generation
prompt: Create a GitHub Actions release workflow that triggers on version tags and runs GoReleaser to produce binaries and a changelog.
trap: Model may use default checkout which does a shallow clone, causing GoReleaser to generate an incomplete or empty changelog

assertions.text: Checkout step uses fetch-depth: 0 for full git history
Workflow triggers on tag push with a v* pattern
Uses contents: write permission for creating releases
Passes GITHUB_TOKEN to GoReleaser

name: action-version-pinning
description: Tests whether third-party actions are pinned to immutable revisions
prompt:
Review this GitHub Actions step and tell me if there are any issues:

```yaml
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@master
  - uses: actions/setup-go@main
    with:
      go-version: stable
```
trap: Major tags are more readable than branches but remain mutable; a supply-chain-sensitive workflow should record a full commit SHA.

assertions.text: Identifies that using @master and @main is wrong and insecure
Recommends pinning each action to a reviewed full commit SHA with a release comment
Explains that branches and tags can move unexpectedly and updates need review

name: automerge-missing-metadata-review
prompt: Review only the merge gate: a bot metadata job has required branch checks and uses `if: update_type != "version-update:semver-major"`. The metadata action can produce an empty update_type. Compare with an otherwise identical explicit minor-or-patch allowlist.

assertions.text: Identifies empty/unrecognized metadata passing the negative check
explains that the positive allowlist rejects it
retains required checks and does not claim the valid allowlist is defective
